title: The tuning-target table (GEN.503): the published statistics the tunable draws are tuned to
note: One entry per published statistic. A tunable row of the possibility tables must have a target here (TargetTable.require). A value measured only in the Solar System is a test-point with the solar_system flag, never a target. Labels: READ, DATA, COMPUTED, 2ND-HAND may be tuned to; SNIPPET, RECALLED and NOT REACHED are listed and never tuned to. Source: docs/design/composition/tunable-gaps.md.

targets.statistic: mean of the reported median of log10 fO2 above the iron-wuestite buffer (dIW) of the rocky material that polluted white dwarfs, 22 values
targets.source: Doyle 2020 Table 1 and Doyle 2023 Table 4 (22 values, 2 upper limits left out): mean -1.25, standard error 0.10 (tunable-gaps.md section 3.2, group3-redox-wd-radio.md; the worker computed it and the tunable-gaps lane re-ran it)
targets.label: COMPUTED
targets.falsifier: a mean of the reported dIW (the draw through the white-dwarf detection model, error model fitted to the whole sample or to the stars with both bounds) more than 2 sigma from -1.25 over 3000 seeds

targets.statistic: sample standard deviation of the reported median dIW over the same 22 polluted white dwarfs
targets.source: Doyle 2020 Table 1 and Doyle 2023 Table 4: sample sd 0.45 (intrinsic about 0.22 from 13 well-constrained stars); sigma = 0.45 / sqrt(2 x 21), computed here
targets.label: COMPUTED
targets.falsifier: a sample sd of the reported dIW (the draw through the white-dwarf detection model with the error fitted to the stars with both bounds) more than 2 sigma from 0.45 over 3000 seeds; the error fitted to the whole sample over-disperses and fails at every width (3.3 sigma at 0.05), so it is not the model this target is tuned with (docs/design/composition/wd-pollution-detection.md)

targets.statistic: median C/O of the giant planets with a retrieved C/O

targets.statistic: mean of log10 of the thorium-to-magnesium ratio over its solar value of thick-disc stars
targets.source: Hypatia Catalog (Hinkel et al. 2014, arXiv 1405.6719; open API retrieved 2026-10), [Th/Mg] of the 32 thick-disc stars with both elements: mean -0.063, sd 0.193; thin disc -0.044 (N=215); the thick-thin offset inside the catalogue is -0.019 (sigma 0.036 = sqrt(0.193^2/32 + 0.153^2/215)) and is added to the solar-twin thin-disc centre of row o1, +0.08 (Botelho 2019, 53 twins, sigma of the mean 0.008): 0.061 (GEN.664)
targets.label: COMPUTED
targets.falsifier: a mean of the drawn log10 Th/Mg more than 2 sigma from 0.061 over 2000 seeds; the value is on the solar-twin scale of row o1, the Hypatia thin-disc statistic (-0.044) being 0.12 dex under it (GEN.664)

targets.statistic: sample standard deviation of log10 of the thorium-to-magnesium ratio over its solar value of thick-disc stars
targets.source: Hypatia Catalog (Hinkel et al. 2014, arXiv 1405.6719; open API retrieved 2026-10), [Th/Mg] of the 32 thick-disc stars with both elements: sd 0.193 (thin disc 0.153, N=215; intrinsic 0.056 in 53 solar twins, Botelho 2019); sigma = 0.193 / sqrt(2 x 31)
targets.label: COMPUTED
targets.falsifier: a sample sd of the drawn log10 Th/Mg more than 2 sigma from 0.193 over 2000 seeds; the catalogue spread includes measurement and catalogue scatter, so 0.193 is an upper bound on the intrinsic width

targets.statistic: mean over simulated Kepler surveys of the slope d log10 R / d log10 P of the radius valley between bare cores and envelope planets, periods 2 to 64 d
targets.source: Petigura et al. 2022 (arXiv:2201.10020): m = dlogRp/dlogP = -0.11 +- 0.02, P 1 to 100 d, M* 0.5 to 1.4 (tunable-gaps-sources/group1-subneptunes.md, READ); the other published slopes -0.09 (+0.02/-0.04) Van Eylen and -0.096 (+0.023/-0.027) Ho and Van Eylen lie inside 1 sigma
targets.label: READ
targets.falsifier: a mean simulated valley slope more than 2 sigma from -0.11 over 24 surveys of 4000 planets (physics/radius_valley.py)

targets.statistic: mean over simulated Kepler surveys of the radius of the valley at a period of 10 d, in units of 6371 km (R_E)
targets.source: Petigura et al. 2022 (arXiv:2201.10020): Rp,0 = 1.84 +- 0.03 R_E (6371 km) at P = 10 d (tunable-gaps-sources/group1-subneptunes.md, READ)
targets.label: READ
targets.falsifier: a mean simulated valley radius at 10 d more than 2 sigma from 1.84 over 24 surveys of 4000 planets

targets.statistic: mean over simulated Kepler surveys of alpha in log10 R_valley = c + alpha log10 F + beta log10 M*, the valley radius against insolation F at a given stellar mass, cells of 0.5 to 1.4 solar masses by 1 to 1000 times a reference insolation (the flux at 1 AU from a 1 solar-mass star)
targets.source: Berger et al. 2023 (arXiv:2302.00009, abstract READ for GEN.722): alpha = 0.069 +0.019 -0.023 (sigma taken as the mean of the two sides); core-powered mass loss predicts 0.08 and photoevaporation 0.12 in the same paper
targets.label: READ
targets.falsifier: a mean simulated alpha more than 2 sigma from 0.069 over 12 surveys of 12000 planets (physics/radius_valley.py mass_slopes_of)

targets.statistic: mean over simulated Kepler surveys of beta in log10 R_valley = c + alpha log10 F + beta log10 M*, the valley radius against stellar mass at a given insolation
targets.source: Berger et al. 2023 (arXiv:2302.00009, abstract READ for GEN.722): beta = -0.046 +0.125 -0.117 (sigma the mean of the two sides). The paper's predictions, core-powered mass loss 0.00 and photoevaporation -0.17, both lie inside 1.1 sigma, so the survey cannot choose the mechanism
targets.label: READ
targets.falsifier: a mean simulated beta more than 2 sigma from -0.046 over 12 surveys of 12000 planets (physics/radius_valley.py mass_slopes_of)

targets.statistic: share of the 21 planets of a homogeneous sample (20 hosts) whose inferred core mass fraction is more than 2 sigma above the star-matched value
targets.source: Plotnykov, Valencia, Ross, Reggiani and Schlaufman 2026 (arXiv:2511.17717 v2; READ in tunable-gaps-sources/group2-delivery-retention.md section 2.5): 21 planets, 20 stars, super-Mercuries fall from four to one (Kepler-107 c); mass-radius scatter alone reproduces the outliers about 15 percent of the time.
